bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: Falun Gong and Victims of Forced Organ Harvesting Protection Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 506.

industries.rationale: The bill would require financial institutions to block property and assets of sanctioned individuals and entities involved in forced organ harvesting.
The bill addresses organ transplantation practices and could affect medical institutions involved in international organ procurement or transplant tourism.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would impose visa restrictions and financial sanctions on foreign individuals involved in forced organ harvesting, particularly targeting persecution of Falun Gong practitioners. It would require the State Department to identify and report on individuals and entities participating in such practices, and would direct the President to block their property and deny them entry to the United States. The bill also calls for annual reports to Congress on implementation.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.title: CLEAR LABELS Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 523.

industries.rationale: The bill concerns prescription drugs and likely imposes labeling or supply-chain requirements on pharmaceutical manufacturers.
Manufacturing is listed as a subject term, suggesting the bill may affect production or labeling obligations for drug makers.
Consumer affairs is a subject term, indicating the bill may affect how prescription drugs are presented or sold to consumers.

bill.plainSummary: The source material provides only the bill number, title (CLEAR LABELS Act), and broad subject terms (consumer affairs, manufacturing, prescription drugs, supply chain). Without the bill text or a more detailed summary, it is not possible to describe what specific changes the bill would make to current law or practice.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who fills a prescription. Anyone who buys things.

districtAwards.description: PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO SUPPORT CLOSING THE BROADBAND AVAILABILITY GAP AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN.THE PROPOSED PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING PLANNING AND PRE-DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES: RESEARCH AND DATA COLLECTION, INCLUDING INITIAL IDENTIFICATION OF UNSERVED LOCATIONS AND UNDERSERVED LOCATIONS CONSISTENT WITH RULES, REGULATIONS, AND PROCESSES COMMISSION HAS ESTABLISHED FOR MAKING DETERMINATIONS IN BROADBAND DATA MAPS; THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PRELIMINARY BUDGET FOR PRE-PLANNING ACTIVITIES; PUBLICATIONS, OUTREACH, AND COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT; PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO POTENTIAL SUBGRANTEES, INCLUDING THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND EVENTS; TRAINING FOR EMPLOYEES OF BROADBAND PROGRAM OR OFFICE OF ELIGIBLE ENTITY OR EMPLOYEES OR POLITICAL SUBDIVISIONS OF ELIGIBLE ENTITY, AND RELATED STAFFING CAPACITY OR CONSULTING OR CONTRACTED SUPPORT TO EFFECTUATE GOALS OF BEAD PROGRAM; ESTABLISHING, OPERATING, OR INCREASING CAPACITY OF A BROADBAND OFFICE THAT OVERSEES BROADBAND PROGRAMS AND BROADBAND DEPLOYMENT IN AN ELIGIBLE ENTITY; ASSET MAPPING ACROSS THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY TO CATALOGUE BROADBAND ADOPTION, AFFORDABILITY, EQUITY, ACCESS AND DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES OCCURRING WITHIN THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY; CONDUCTING SURVEYS OF UNSERVED, UNDERSERVED, AND UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND BARRIERS TO ADOPTION; REASONABLE POST-NOFO, PRE-AWARD EXPENSES IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $100,000 RELATING TO THE PREPARATION OF PROGRAM SUBMISSIONS TO NTIA (SUCH AS THE LETTER OF INTENT) OR ADDING ADDITIONAL CAPACITY TO STATE OR TERRITORIAL BROADBAND OFFICES IN PREPARATION FOR THE BEAD PROGRAM MAY BE REIMBURSED IF THEY ARE INCURRED AFTER THE PUBLICATION DATE OF THIS NOFO AND PRIOR TO THE DATE OF ISSUANCE OF THE GRANT AWARD FROM NTIA, EXCEPT THAT LOBBYING COSTS AND CONTINGENCY FEES ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE FROM GRANT FUNDS; AND COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH MEETING THE LOCAL COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS IN SECTION IV.C.1.C OF THIS NOFO INCLUDING CAPACITY BUILDING AT THE LOCAL AND REGIONAL LEVELS OR CONTRACTED SUPPORT. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE OUTCOMES OF WISCONSIN'S PROPOSED PROJECT ARE A FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN, SEQUENCING CONCURRENTLY WITH WISCONSIN'S DIGITAL EQUITY PLAN AND INCORPORATING OUTREACH AND FOCUSED UNDERSTANDING OF COMMUNITIES FACING UNDUE BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATION IN THE DIGITAL COMMUNITY, IMPLEMENTING A FIVE-YEAR BUILDOUT OF  BROADBAND INFRASTRUCTURE SO THAT ALL WISCONSINITES MAY REALIZE MEANINGFUL CONNECTION TO OUR DIGITAL WORLD, A LOCALLY INFORMED ANALYSIS OF BROADBAND NEEDS IN EACH REGION THAT WILL SERVE AS THE BASIS OF THE STATEWIDE PLAN;  IMPROVED CAPACITY FOR LOCAL LEADERS TO FACILITATE BROADBAND PLANNING, ENSURING EXPEDITIOUS ALLOCATION OF FUNDING THAT ALIGNS WITH THE VISION AND NEEDS OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES; INCREASED LOCAL CAPACITY AND MOMENTUM FOR BROADBAND PLANNING, AND A CLEAR VISION FROM LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO INFORM THE FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN; COLLECTION OF GRANULAR SERVICE AND AFFORDABILITY DATA, INCORPORATION OF DATA INTO PUBLIC-FACING VISUALIZATIONS, AND ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY SERVICE GAPS AND IMPLEMENT DEPLOYMENT EFFORTS; RECOMMENDATIONS, PILOT PROGRAMS, AND A PLAN TO ENSURE A DIVERSE WORKFORCE READY TO DESIGN, DEPLOY, AND MAINTAIN A ROBUST STATEWIDE BROADBAND NETWORK; AND A COMPREHENSIVE PROGRAM AND BUDGET THAT IS EFFICIENT, TRANSPARENT, FEDERALLY COMPLIANT, COLLABORATIVELY SEQUENCED WITH DIGITAL EQUITY EFFORTS, AND READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE UNSERVED AND UNDERSERVED GROUPS IN THE STATE OF WISCONSIN WITH A FOCUS ON RURAL AND UNSERVED POPULATIONS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THE RECIPIENT DOES NOT INTEND TO SUBAWARD FUNDS.
